subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should scoped ACP permission defaults be exposed as generic permissionProfile defaults on bindings[].acp and agents.list[].runtime.acp, as ACPX-specific permissionMode/nonInteractivePermissions keys, or not exposed as static config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public shape controls write and shell authority for non-interactive ACP sessions and could either align with generic ACP runtime options or create a backend-specific parallel config surface.

options.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
options.body: Add scoped permissionProfile defaults that flow through the existing ACP runtime option layer, keeping ACPX-specific permissionMode names at the plugin-global layer.

options.title: Add ACPX-specific scoped keys
options.body: Implement the requested permissionMode and optional nonInteractivePermissions precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific public config surface.

options.title: Keep global config only
options.body: Document global ACPX config and live ACP runtime controls as the supported paths, leaving static scoped permission defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use generic permissionProfile defaults
recommendation.body: Add scoped permissionProfile defaults that flow through the existing ACP runtime option layer, keeping ACPX-specific permissionMode names at the plugin-global layer.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the ACP runtime option shape and ACPX integration history most likely to define the durable permission contract.
